articleTitle: Angle-of-Arrival (AoA) Estimation using Dual-Frequency Band FMCW Radar Systems
abstract: The angle-of-arrival (AoA) estimation is essential in various applications, including wireless communications and radar systems. This study proposes a novel method for AoA estimation using dual-frequency differential phase contrast analysis in uniform and non-uniform linear arrays of a frequency-modulated continuous-wave (FMCW) radar system. Using the differential phase contrast of the dual-frequency channels, the proposed method not only effectively resolves ambiguities arising from antenna spacing greater than half wavelength but also enhances the accuracy and robustness of AoA estimation. Extensive simulations and measurements data validate the effectiveness of the proposed technique in precisely estimating the arrival direction of the signals in real-world scenarios.

articleTitle: Dual Linearly Polarized 76-81 GHz Automotive Antenna System Concept for Street Condition Monitoring
abstract: Street condition monitoring (SCM) is a relatively new application that is deemed crucial to achieve the next level of safety in autonomous driving (AD). Currently, there are no radar sensors in the market that provide classification for all types of street conditions due to the high RCS-sensitivity requirements and the need for dedicated monolithic microwave integrated circuit (MMIC) channels. In this publication, a novel system concept is presented that integrates street condition monitoring into a radar system comprising two antenna systems: one looking at the bore-sight and the other towards the street. The supplementary dual linearly polarized antenna system is capable of detecting all types of streets and conditions with very high dynamic range and maximum sensitivity. Unique design exigencies such as gain, antenna polarization purity, and the elevation beam tilt needed for the detection of sensitive street returns at incidence angles feasible for dual polarization classification are presented.

articleTitle: A TRL-based Measurement Technique for the Characterization of RF Current Probes
abstract: RF current probes can be used for inductive measurement or injection of interference currents on wires during operation. As such, current probes are frequently used in the domain of electromagnetic compatibility (EMC) testing, and there in particular for automotive applications. In order to determine the S-parameters of a current probe, it is common to de-embed an equivalent circuit of the test fixture, with circuit elements obtained by fitting. Instead of de-embedding, this present paper proposes a modified thru-reflect-line (TRL) self-calibration procedure to determine and to correct for the linear error terms of the EMC test fixture. The modification of TRL is necessary because a current probe is a 3-port which connects a coaxial port to two “wire above ground” ports with different port impedances. Measurement results of S-parameters of an RF current probe obtained by the two methods up to 1 GHz are presented and discussed.

articleTitle: Dual Frequency SIW Longitudinal Slot Array Antenna for Automotive Radar Application: Configurable FOV and Gain
abstract: This paper presents the design and analysis of a single-layer substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) longitudinal slot array antenna, optimized for high gain and low Side Lobe Levels (SLL) in the $\mathbf{W}$-band frequency. The antenna achieves a gain difference of over 3 dB between 76.5 GHz and 79 GHz, facilitated by a custom-designed filter with one input and four outputs. The design incorporates four arrays, each consisting of six slots, with radiation energy governed by the slots’ length and offset. Dolph-Chebyshev tapering is employed to improve sidelobe performance, leading to a substantial enhancement in bandwidth and an overall gain increase of 4.6 dB. This technique provides a high gain that extends the detection range at higher frequency band and a wider azimuth field-of-view (FOV) at lower frequency band.

articleTitle: Over-the-Air Synchronization of Automotive Distributed Radar Networks by Using 3D-Printed Antennas
abstract: In this work, two possibilities for over-the-air synchronization of distributed radar systems are evaluated in simulation. Therefore, a direct path between the radar nodes is used to establish a reference link by which all necessary parameters can be estimated. Additionally, a synchronization with less effort but using a target is compared. Simulations show that both synchronization techniques can achieve a coherent antenna array through signal processing. Additionally, a 3D-printed antenna is proposed to enable a direct path between the radar nodes.

articleTitle: On the Necessity of In-Situ Impedance Measurements in the High Frequency Range
abstract: This contribution discusses the necessity of new in-situ measurement approaches to determine system parameters for an effective EMC-compliant system design in future power electronic systems. Due to the high switching speeds and steep switching edges of new wide-band-gap semiconductors, the electromagnetic interference (EMI) spectrum is shifting towards higher frequencies. In a practical measurement setup the EMI potential of such a device is analyzed and difficulties in measuring the impedance and thus extracting the system properties in the higher frequency range is addressed.

articleTitle: PAPR Reduction Using Invasive Weed Optimization Algorithm in FBMC-OQAM Systems
abstract: Modern communication systems are continuously advancing to satisfy the requirements for broadband data transmission and minimal latency. A pivotal aspect of this progress is the Filter Bank MultiCarrier-Offset Quadrature Amplitude Modulation (FBMC-OQAM) system, which represents a novel approach in wireless communication. Nevertheless, a significant challenge of the FBMC-OQAM system is its high peak-to-average-power-ratio (PAPR). Elevated PAPR levels increase the complexity of hardware and induce nonlinearities in high-power amplifiers (HPA), ultimately impairing the quality of the transmitted signal. The nonlinear effects resulting from high PAPR can cause spectral regrowth and interference with adjacent channels, further degrading system performance. Therefore, addressing the issue of high PAPR is crucial for the practical implementation of FBMC-OQAM systems. Various strategies have been proposed to reduce PAPR, within clipping and filtering, selective mapping (SLM), and partial transmit sequences (PTS). In this research, the PTS technique is augmented with the Invasive Weed Optimization (IWO) algorithm to effectively minimize PAPR. The IWO algorithm, inspired by the colonization behavior of invasive weeds in nature, enhances the PTS method’s efficiency by optimizing phase factor selection. The integration of IWO with PTS not only addresses the high PAPR problem but also presents a promising solution for the practical deployment of FBMC-OQAM systems in next-generation communication networks. In the simulations, the number of subcarriers $\mathbf{N}$ and the population size W were varied to derive results, illustrating the relationship between the PAPR threshold $P A P R_{0}$ and the CCDF. The CCDF is defined by $\operatorname{Pr}\left[P A P R\gt P A P R_{0}\right]$. The most favorable results were obtained for N = 32, where the PAPR of the original FBMC-OQAM signal was 12.66 dB, reduced to 9.93 dB by the PTS method, and further decreased to 8.4 dB by the IWO algorithm, demonstrating the superior effectiveness of the combined approach. Particularly noteworthy are the peak performances observed for $N=(32,64,128,256,512)$ where the corresponding PAPR values for the IWO algorithm were 8.4 $\mathrm{dB}, 9.2 \mathrm{~dB}, 9.8 \mathrm{~dB}, 10.23 \mathrm{~dB}$ and 11 dB respectively. This notable outcome highlights the efficacy and adaptability of the proposed hybrid approach, paving the way for the seamless integration of FBMC-OQAM systems into future communication infrastructures.

Author Keywords: Partial Transmit Sequence (PTS) Invasive Weed Optimization (IWO)

articleTitle: Non-linear Filtering Techniques for Improving Accurate Vehicle Angle Determination
abstract: Accurate measurement of vehicle angles, particularly pitch angles, is crucial for the safety and efficiency of modern vehicles. These angles affect vehicle dynamics such as acceleration and braking and are essential for adaptive headlight systems that adjust lighting based on vehicle pitch. Various methods exist for measuring vehicle pitch angles, including LiDAR, wheel sensors combined with inclinometers, and inertial measurement units or accelerometers in conjunction with wheel sensors. A cost-effective approach employs an algorithm that calculates real acceleration from vehicle speed and accounts for road inclination using only accelerometers. However, this algorithm only provides reliable results with accurate accelerometer data. Since accelerometers are prone to noise, signal processing requires filtering. Linear filters, which significantly smooth the signal, are unsuitable here as they can distort crucial signal information through over-smoothing. Instead, nonlinear filters offer a better solution. The Kuwahara filter, total variation filter, and bilateral filter are such nonlinear alternatives that reduce noise while preserving essential signal details, such as edges and features. Tests indicate that without adequate filtering, the average deviation in pitch angle is 1.4 degrees, with a maximum error of 19.4 degrees. With the use of the bilateral filter, this average error is reduced to 0.11 degrees and the maximum error to 1.2 degrees.

articleTitle: Frequency-Dependent RCS Characterization of a CRLH-Based Leaky Wave Antenna
abstract: An impedance loading method for separating radiation and structure scattering components is proposed and utilized to characterize the frequency-dependent radiation radar cross section (RCS) of a composite right-/left-handed (CRLH) microstrip-based leaky wave antenna (LWA). A specific set of backscattered fields of the CRLH LWA arising from termination with short and open load impedance are used to express the structure mode and radiation (antenna) mode scattered fields of the CRLH LWA. The contribution of each mode to the total scattering fields is properly analysed, which reveals the frequency dependence of the horizontally polarized radiation mode of the CRLH LWA. The proposed procedure is demonstrated by analyzing a prototypical CRLH LWA demonstrating its effectiveness.

articleTitle: Analysis of 60 GHz Radar Channel Characteristics in Indoor and Outdoor Environments
abstract: Robust indoor detection of moving objects is crucial for monitoring critical safety aspects. In addition to the radar hardware, the limitations are primarily influenced by the channel propagation characteristics, such as multipath propagation. This paper presents the modeling and analysis of channel characterization for two indoor and one outdoor setup using a 60 GHz FMCW radar. The channel analysis is achieved through ray tracing and measurements. The simulation results compare the channel spread in densely and sparsely configured indoor environments with that of an outdoor environment. A significant correlation is observed between the simulation results and the measurements. The results of the indoor analysis demonstrate different multipath reflections. Point cloud behavior is noted in the densely configured setup, whereas discrete multipath propagation occurs in the spacious setup. The analysis of the received power delay spread is illustrated, highlighting the limitations of radar sensing in indoor environments.

articleTitle: Volume Structure Retrieval over Vegetated Areas Using a Pair of Synthetic Aperture Radar Images with Wide Fractional Bandwidth
abstract: This paper presents a novel method which uses the frequency-dependent coherence of interferometric synthetic aperture radar (InSAR) data to invert the volume structure of vegetated areas. The method uses a pair of synthetic aperture radar (SAR) images with wide fractional bandwidths, which are available from radars mounted on drones. The random-volume-over-ground (RVoG) model, which assumes a homogeneous volume over a rough surface, is widely used in the InSAR remote sensing community to characterize semi-transparent media such as forests and vegetation. Semi-transparent media assuming RVoG scenarios are inverted using frequency-dependent coherence measurements. A method to generate simulated radar data for RVoG scenarios is presented and the inversion results are discussed.

articleTitle: A Function Generator on TSMC 65nm CMOS for Analog Computing
abstract: This paper presents a detailed analysis of a function generator that utilizes a fully differential analog input processed through a current subtractor, offset comparators, thermometercoded current steering X-iDAC, programmable ROM, 11-to-32 decoder and Y-iDAC. This configuration enables precise and customizable waveform generation, crucial for various applications in analog computing and signal processing.

articleTitle: An Approach for SI-Compliant Parameter Space Evaluation Using a Decision Tree-Based AI Module
abstract: The application of high-speed systems is associated with a high degree of design complexity. In particular, maintaining the signal integrity (SI) must be ensured by detailed simulations using EDA design environments. The PCB designer has to find suitable parameter combinations for the transmission line networks under consideration in order to obtain adequate signal quality. AI-based optimization methods such as Bayesian optimization (BO) or genetic algorithm (GA) can already be found in literature for speeding up SI compliant design. Nevertheless, these algorithms can become very complex for a large number of design parameters and the given AI solutions must be accepted without insight. To overcome these challenges, this contribution presents an approach based on the combination of a decision tree (DT) and a support vector regression (SVR) surrogate model. The parameter space available to the PCB designer is first evaluated and SI-compliant parameter sets are predicted using the combined DT/SVR module. Finally, an optimal parameter space is obtained by evaluating the marginal probability mass functions (marginal PMFs) of the SI-conform combinations. The traceable structure of the decision tree in conjunction with the statistical evaluation enables the PCB designer to understand the DT/SVR module’s proposals in order to make the final decision.

articleTitle: Enhanced Wind Turbine Detection through Radar and Radiometric Sensor Fusion
abstract: This paper introduces an overview of a novel sensor fusion model for identifying wind turbines (WTs) that cause interference in polarimetric Doppler weather radar measurements. It is important to acknowledge that the characteristics of WTs, as defined by their radar cross section (RCS), have a substantial effect on radar performance. This is because the RCS of WTs leads to the introduction of multidimensional interference effects, which ultimately influence radar measurements. This interference is due to the incident electromagnetic fields that it interacts with a WT, which, in turn, generates both static and dynamic effects. In the realm of electromagnetic wave-matter interactions, the effective permittivity $\varepsilon_{e f f}$ is composed of two significant aspects: the real part $\varepsilon^{\prime}$ and the imaginary part $\varepsilon^{\prime \prime}$. In this context, passive satellite, also known as a radiometer provides sensor data (e.g. Sentinel-2 (S2)) that will be employed to accurately identify WTs causing interference to within the radar data. This is because the different effects of the real and imaginary components in metallic objects and the Earth’s surface can be utilized to derive distinct radiometric satellite observables from the given S2 data. These radiometric observables lend themselves to serve as novel Wind Turbine Indices (WTI). Additionally, physical quantities such as emissivity $\epsilon_{\lambda}$ and albedo $\rho_{\text {albedo }}$, which describe thermal radiation properties and reflectivity of surfaces, will be evaluated and applied to WT detection.

articleTitle: B-Spline-Based Higher-Order Discretization of the Magnetic Field Integral Equation
abstract: The hitherto first conforming higher-order discretization of the magnetic field integral equation (MFIE) is presented. Non-conforming discretizations of the MFIE lead to a loss of accuracy and make it impossible to obtain low-frequency stable formulations. So far, however, only a lowest-order conforming discretization of the MFIE has been presented by leveraging Buffa-Christiansen (BC) functions, which are dual to the lowest-order Rao-Wilton-Glisson (RWG) functions, limiting the speed of convergence. We obtain a conforming high-order discretization by utilizing B-spline-based basis functions and establishing a set of dual basis functions, which can be regarded as a generalization of the (low-order) BC functions known from triangular meshes. Numerical results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed discretization scheme.

articleTitle: Building a simple oscillator based Ising machine for research and education
abstract: Oscillator based Ising machines are non-von-Neumann machines ideally suited for solving combinatorial problems otherwise intractable on classic stored-program digital computers due to their run-time complexity. Possible future applications are manifold ranging from quantum simulations to protein folding and are of high academic and commercial interest as well. Described in the following is a very simple such machine aimed at educational and research applications.

articleTitle: Comparison of Feeding Network Topologies in Air Waveguide Slot Array Antennas for Automotive Radar Applications at 79 GHz
abstract: In this study, three different feed networks for air waveguide slot array antenna structures are introduced: side-fed, middle series feeding networks, and semi middle series feed networks. Middle series networks provide precise control over phase and amplitude due to their central placement of the feeding network. Conversely, side-fed configurations may have limited control over mutual coupling and phase alignment among array elements but offer spatial efficiency compared to middle fed setups. In the third design, a synthesis of both structures’ advantages is achieved: the middle fed structure enables amplitude and phase adjustments for each slot, while the side fed design minimizes spatial occupation compared to the middle fed series feed network.

articleTitle: A MEMS-Based GPS-Disciplined Oscillator for Mobile RF Measurement Applications
abstract: Many spatially distributed radio frequency (RF) measurement setups require coherence, i.e., synchronization of their local oscillators (LOs). In static setups, this can be achieved by distributing a common reference clock signal over a wired cable infrastructure. In mobile setups without wired infrastructure, synchronization can be achieved using global positioning system (GPS)-disciplined oscillators (GPSDOs). However, those typically incorporate rather bulky crystal oscillators, which are inherently sensitive to mechanical stress, i.e., vibration and temperature fluctuation. In contrast, micro-electromechanical system (MEMS) oscillators are less sensitive to environmental influences, while maintaining a small footprint. This paper presents a compact MEMS-based GPSDO concept with real-time kinematic (RTK) support for mobile applications. Measurements for short-and long-term frequency stability of the fabricated design are shown.

articleTitle: Varicose-mode Events - Two Case Studies
abstract: A recent study analyzed MAARSY data from seven PMSE seasons (May-August, 2015-2021), revealing frequent occurrences of varicose structures, with a 2.5% monthly occurrence rate - some of them include extreme vertical velocities. The study identified more than 700 varicose-mode events covering about 265 hours of data. While varicose structures occur relatively frequently, extreme vertical velocities above the $3 \sigma$ threshold are rare. The causes of these events remain unclear despite statistical analysis. Integrating data from the SIMONe network, and additional MAARSY observations, the study focuses on high vertical velocity cases to understand the ambient conditions underlying these unique events, enhancing our understanding of middle atmosphere dynamics.

articleTitle: Radar imaging device using prism shaped aperture
abstract: An inspection system utilizing millimeter wave imaging is presented. It performs 3D imaging with an inverse synthetic aperture approach. The object under test is passing on a conveyor belt while being investigated with millimeter waves. The system seeks to overcome the limitations of a planar aperture and enables a prism-shaped aperture which is richer in terms of angular illumination. Real-time processing is possible through an integrated industrial GPU. To process the images from raw reflection data, a hybrid algorithm, combining elements of backprojection and the Omega-k algorithm, is derived. This algorithm unites the flexibility of backprojection with the computational advantages of the Omega-k algorithm. The system utilizes commercially available radar MMICs working from 57 to $\mathbf{6 4} \mathbf{G H z}$. Exemplary imaging results are shown and a comparison with backprojection is drawn.

articleTitle: A Low-cost X-band Active Front-end Module for Weather Applications
abstract: Dense networks of weather micro radars are optimally suited to yield enhanced sounding of the lower troposphere. However, sustainable instantiation requires leveraging on electronic beam steering within a cost-constrained design in order to reach a point of competition with traditional mechanically steered solutions. Implementation and instrumental validation of an active front-end module for monoaxial beam steering at X-band is detailed as a key component to assess feasibility.

articleTitle: Distributed UAV-SAR: System Concept Overview and Error Model
abstract: Technological advances have opened up the possibility to combine small unmanned aerial vehicles (UAV) and radar sensors. In this paper, a novel, multistatic system concept is presented that incorporates several identical, fully digital, multichannel radar sensors carried by UAV platforms. Each single radar is implemented in a direct sampling architecture on an AMD Zynq Ultrascale+ RF System on Chip (RFSoC), and all processing steps are performed in the digital domain, offering a high level of flexibility to the system. The system is currently being build up and intended primarily to serve as a research and development platform for the exploration of new multistatic synthetic aperture radar (SAR) imaging modes and techniques such as single-pass tomography, multi-baseline interferometry and holography, as well as new acquisition modes and techniques for future NewSpace SAR missions. Due to the individual local oscillators in each radar unit, accurate time, frequency and phase synchronisation is crucial for achieving a good multistatic measurement and imaging performance. An error model as well as the results of first ground-based experiments will be presented for mono- and multistatic measurements with the digital radars.

articleTitle: 3D FEM simulation of biological cells in heterogeneous alternating electric fields
abstract: This work presents an algorithm that can be used to numerically calculate force and torque on which dielectrophoresis and electrorotation are based and approximate the resulting translation and rotation of biological cells in heterogenous, alternating electric fields. A two-stage simulation on different levels is used for calculation, which is based on the finite element method. A 3D cell model with arbitrary geometry is utilized. Due to considerable differences in scale in the cell model, a domain decomposition algorithm with overlapping auxiliary domains for coupling is applied. An electro-quasistatic model equation is used to determine the electrical scalar potential inside the cell model. Based on this, force and torque can be calculated and the equations of motion can be approximated using a second-order time stepping method. The algorithm is validated with analytical reference models and shows a high level of accuracy.

articleTitle: Radar Target Generation for Angular Resolution Testing in a Compact Test Range with Two Antennas
abstract: This work presents a ray-tracing simulation approach for an automotive compact radar test range. The goal is to generate two targets separated in azimuthal direction to test the angular resolution of a radar under test. The setup is programmed as a ray-tracer in Matlab, with the application of a wave function to the rays. The effects which occur due to the offset of the antennas from the focus point are analyzed. The system is realized with movable antennas to enable different angular distances.

articleTitle: Angle-of-Arrival (AoA) Estimation in Dual-Frequency Band FMCW Radar Systems Using Range and Doppler Dependent Calibration
abstract: This study presents a novel approach for angle-of-arrival (AoA) estimation in dual-frequency band frequency-modulated continuous wave (FMCW) radar systems through range and Doppler dependent calibration. Building upon our previous research, the study addresses challenges associated with phase coherence between antenna arrays operating at different frequencies. The proposed methodology involves an initial calibration to determine the phase offsets, followed by the creation of a lookup table based on target range and Doppler. Simulation and measurement results demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach in AoA estimation, improving the angular accuracy and resolution of the radar system.

articleTitle: Solving Electromagnetic Scattering Problems by Isogeometric Analysis with Deep Operator Learning
abstract: We present a hybrid approach combining isogeometric analysis with deep operator networks to solve electromagnetic scattering problems. The neural network takes a computer aided design representation as input and predicts the electromagnetic field in a de Rham conforming B-spline basis such that for example the tangential continuity of the electric field is respected. The physical problem is included in the loss function during training. Our numerical results demonstrate that a trained network accurately predicts the electric field, showing convergence to the analytical solution with optimal rate. Additionally, training on a variety of geometries highlights the network’s generalization capabilities, achieving small error increases when applied to new geometries not included in the training set.

articleTitle: Angle-dependent scattering properties of the skin at the human lower arm at THz frequencies
abstract: Electromagnetic radiation in the terahertz range has specific properties which can be utilized for medical applications. Terahertz radiation enables high spatial resolution and is non-ionizing. Terahertz technology is already being used for the analysis of transmission and reflection properties of biological tissues. Due to the high water content in human skin which is highly absorptive for terahertz radiation, the skin can only be investigated in reflection mode. The reflection properties and refractive index of human skin have already been described in literature. Nearly all previous studies were conducted at a fixed incident angle of the terahertz beam or with skin which was pressed against a flat surface. The scattering effects of human skin in the terahertz range are still largely unknown. In this work, we employ a terahertz frequency-domain spectroscopy system in a quasi-monostatic configuration to measure the reflection properties of the skin of the forearm at frequencies around 100 GHz. The measurement is non-invasive, contactless and is conducted for different incident angles.

articleTitle: Tomographic ISAR imaging of satellites: A ground-based experimental validation
abstract: As the number of parties with access to Earth’s orbit increases, more low-cost satellites with only limited onboard diagnostic tools are brought into orbit. As a service to satellite operators an external imaging of satellites in space would give valuable information. Additionally, a tight observation of satellites is of international interest. An experimental radar system called IoSiS (Imaging of Satellites in Space) was developed at the German Aerospace Center (DLR) and is capable of delivering high resolution 2-dimensional radar images. For a more thorough observation and an easier interpretation of the collected images, the IoSiS project is moving towards complete and true 3-dimensional imaging through the use of distributed receivers. Here, theoretical analysis is shown to gain first insights into synthetic aperture radar (SAR) tomography in this new context. A new ground-based system for demonstration purposes is developed from the ground up, and is able to perform tomographic imaging. The newly developed system is FPGA based, and implements a new state-of-the-art system-on-a-chip. Interpretation of the gathered 3-dimensional measurements and multiple visualization approaches are shown and tested.

articleTitle: High Temperature In-Order RISC-V Processor with Heterogeneous Pipeline and Out-of-Order Write-Back Mechanism
abstract: Modern deep drilling operations depend on a complex network of sensors, actuators, and controllers installed at the drill string’s bottom end. These electronic components must withstand extreme conditions, including temperatures up to $175^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$ and pressures reaching 200 MPa. Due to the lack of fast communication to the surface, autonomous in situ digital signal processing is essential. To address these challenges, a high-performance RISC-V processor has been developed, capable of reliable operation in such harsh environments. The XT018 180 nanometer Silicon-on-Insulator (SOI) process from XFAB was selected for its advanced capabilities, ensuring the production of robust electronic circuits suited for these extreme conditions. [1]. Conventional RISC-V architectures typically employ a five-stage pipeline design, which constrains the execution phase to a single stage and limits digital signal processing (DSP) capabilities. To address this, the custom RISC-V processor features a heterogeneous execution pipeline, with unit delays ranging from one cycle to 29 cycles [2]. This instruction-dependent pipeline length enables the RV32IMCF processor to achieve clock speeds of up to 180 MHz for $175^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$ with is up to 4 times higher than typical processors in similar application specific integrated circuit (ASIC) technologies [3], [4]. To further enhance performance, this new contribution introduces out-of-order writebacks and a split writeback mechanism that operates independently from the issue stage. These innovations effectively manage Write After Write (WAW) hazards and general hazard detection, maintaining reliable operation. The design ensures that multiple instructions executed by the same unit remain in order. Synchronization of the asymmetric processor execution stages is managed through handshakes, which, while adding control logic to each execution unit, relieve the controller of significant workload. Compared to an RV32IMFC processor limited to single-cycle execution stages, this advanced design achieves up to 18 times higher clock frequencies. Additionally, the out-of-order writebacks and split independent writeback mechanism deliver at least a 5% performance boost over previous designs, with potential improvements of up to 50% in benchmarks that fully exploit these capabilities, showcasing substantial enhancements in processing efficiency and throughput.

articleTitle: Street Condition Monitoring with Automotive Dual Linearly Polarized Radar System: Measurement Results and Classification
abstract: This publication presents an innovative automotive radar system designed for street condition monitoring (SCM). To demonstrate the performance of the system, various street conditions and types such as dry asphalt, wet asphalt, snow-covered asphalt, concrete, grass, and cobblestone have been measured. These data have been cross-validated with the data from the literature. The SCM system integrates dedicated monolithic microwave integrated circuit (MMIC) and multiple-input and multiple-output (MIMO) channels, enabling full polarimetric capabilities for real-time street classification. Our analysis supports the simulation results and demonstrates the effectiveness of street type and condition classification. By presenting the measured data and a classification method, this study advances the field of street condition monitoring for improved vehicle safety.

articleTitle: Long-term changes of mesosphere/lower thermosphere gravity waves over Collm, Germany
abstract: Time series of mesosphere/lower thermosphere half-hourly winds over Collm ($51.3^{\circ} \mathrm{N}, 13.0^{\circ}$ E) have been obtained from 1984-2007 by low frequency (LF) spaced receiver measurements and from 2004 to date by very high frequency (VHF) meteor radar Doppler wind observations in the height range 82-97 km. These observations are analysed with respect to gravity wave (GW) climatology and trends. From half-hourly differences of zonal and meridional winds, GW variance proxies have been calculated that describe amplitude variations in the period range 1-3 hours. After applying corrections to account for instrumental differences, the GW climatology and time series have been obtained. The mean GW activity in the upper mesosphere shows maximum amplitudes in summer, while in the lower thermosphere GWs maximize in winter. At altitudes around 90 km, positive/negative long-term trends are visible in winter/summer. In the lower thermosphere, however, long-term amplitude trends are generally positive. Quasi-decadal variations of GW amplitudes and mean winds are also visible, showing a possible influence of the 11-year solar cycle. Interannual wind and GW variations show a possible influence of lower atmosphere circulation patterns.

articleTitle: Analysis of the Bias Voltage Dependency of the Efficiency of a Schottky Diode-Based Harmonic Millimeter-Wave Transponder Tag
abstract: A harmonic radar (HR) consists of a transceiver and a transponder tag. The transponder tag in a passive harmonic radar consists of a nonlinear element such as a Schottky diode and a resonator like an antenna. One of the most important features of a passive transponder tag is its small volume. By increasing the operating frequency to the millimeter-wave band, the tag can be made small enough to be mounted on a honey bee without hindering its movement. Therefore, in this work, the operating frequency is 50 GHz and the second harmonic is generated by a Schottky diode at 100 GHz. The nonlinear element in a passive transponder tag is usually chosen as a zero bias Schottky diode. However, impedance matching between antenna and Schottky diode at zero bias can be problematic. The objective of this paper is to analyze the dependency of the conversion efficiency of a passive tag on the bias voltage of the Schottky diode under optimum matching conditions.

articleTitle: ESPARGOS: Phase-Coherent WiFi CSI Datasets for Wireless Sensing Research
abstract: The use of WiFi signals to sense the physical environment is gaining popularity, with some common applications being motion detection and transmitter localization. Standardcompliant WiFi provides a cost effective, easy and backward-compatible approach to Joint Communication and Sensing and enables a seamless transfer of results from experiments to practical applications. However, most WiFi sensing research is conducted on channel state information (CSI) data from current-generation devices, which are usually not meant for sensing applications and thus lack sufficient spatial diversity or phase synchronization. With ESPARGOS, we previously developed a phase-coherent, real-time capable many-antenna WiFi channel sounder specifically for wireless sensing. We describe how we use ESPARGOS to capture large CSI datasets that we make publicly available. The datasets are extensively documented and labeled, for example with information from reference positioning systems, enabling data-driven and machine learning-based research.

articleTitle: Phase Synchronization Concept for the Bistatic Extension of the Airborne F-SAR System
abstract: The requirements for future synthetic aperture radar (SAR) systems are evolving towards bistatic and multistatic acquisition modes with distributed transmitter and receiver systems. However, due to the underlying physics in the radar signal processing, especially for SAR interferometry, phase coherence and hence phase synchronization are essential for the development of such systems. This work analyses and proposes an optical synchronization link for the bistatic extension of the existing airborne SAR system, called F-SAR [1] from the German Aerospace Center at L-band frequencies $(\mathbf{1. 3 2 5 ~ G H z})$. The use of time-to-digital converters reduces the complexity of the system, the data rate, and the frequency interference in comparison to existing methods and provides a general approach to synchronize without committing to a specific microwave frequency range. To prove the feasibility, a custom RF-measurement board is developed and hardware tests are performed in the laboratory achieving phase synchronization better than $\pm 5 \mathrm{ps}\left(\pm 2.5^{\circ}\right)$.

articleTitle: Separation of Scattering Mechanisms Through Multiple-Input Multiple-Output Synthetic Aperture Radar Tomography
abstract: Synthetic aperture radar (SAR) tomography is gaining increasing interest for its capability to reconstruct the vertical profile of natural and urban scenes. However, since large tomographic apertures will be used in the future in order to increase the vertical resolution of the three-dimensional reconstruction, an analysis of the far-field approximation is necessary to assess its validity in SAR tomography. In addition, it is of great importance to understand how different scattering mechanisms behave based on the selected tomographic SAR acquisition configuration. Multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) SAR tomography has been proven to be able to detect and separate the contribution of single- and double-bounce scattering, allowing a more precise vertical reconstruction of the scene, and this capability will be assessed in an experiment with a MIMO measurement setup.
